context_requirements: Active nucleotide salvage and de novo purine/pyrimidine synthesis pathways
Proliferating cells with high demand for nucleotide precursors
Intact p53 pathway for full transcriptional response to nucleotide stress
Expression of the targeted dehydrogenases (HPRT1, IMPDH1, PPAT)
falsifiers: No change in expression of nucleotide biosynthesis genes (e.g., IMPDH1, PPAT, HPRT1) at 6 or 24 h
Lack of antiproliferative or apoptotic signature at 24 h in all nine cell lines
Predominant upregulation of cell cycle genes rather than downregulation
No evidence of UPR or stress response activation at 24 h

evidence.supports: LDH inhibition blocks glycolysis and ATP production, leading to growth inhibition and stress responses in breast cancer cells
LDHA inhibition suppresses tumor growth and induces mitochondria-mediated apoptosis via ROS
DHODH inhibition induces apoptosis and G1 cell cycle arrest in multiple myeloma cells
IMPDH inhibition by 6-azauracil causes sensitivity in yeast mutants, implicating nucleotide depletion and transcriptional stress
IMPDH inhibition depletes GTP, induces caspase-dependent apoptosis and G1-S arrest in multiple myeloma cells

changes: Removed HPRT1 from proximal_up: inhibiting HPRT1 should not increase its own transcription; direction not justified.
Removed MYC from proximal_up: MYC is a proliferation driver and is listed as down in proximal_down; a dehydrogenase inhibitor causing nucleotide stress would not proximally upregulate MYC.
Removed duplicate MYC from proximal_down? No, kept MYC only in proximal_down to avoid appearing in both up and down lists at the same time.

Removed generic proliferation/stress genes from proximal lists where they are not proximal to dehydrogenase inhibition: MYC, DDIT4, TRIB3, ATF5, ASCC3, XBP1, HERPUD1, DNAJB1, HSPA1A, SQSTM1, CHAC1, TXNRD1 were retained only if stress/UPR-related; MYC removed from proximal_up.
Kept late_up stress/UPR genes as downstream consequences of nucleotide depletion and metabolic stress.
Kept late_down cell cycle genes consistent with G1/S and G2/M arrest after nucleotide depletion.
No line_response changes: no abstract evidence contradicts the moderate/weak assignments for the nine lines.
No kinetics or magnitude changes: slow kinetics and weak 6 h/moderate 24 h are consistent with nucleotide depletion and delayed transcriptional stress responses.

Evidence kept only where abstracts support the stated claim; all five cited abstracts support dehydrogenase inhibition causing growth inhibition, apoptosis, cell cycle arrest, or nucleotide-stress transcriptional effects.
